# Liquid thermal conductivity from the Pedersen (PFCT) correlation

`eos.thermal_conductivity`

## Source

**NeqSim 3.20.0 `PFCTConductivityMethodMod86`**

`calcConductivity` and `getRefComponentConductivity`, ported verbatim

DOI: [10.1063/1.555828](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.555828)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank with the keycard's overrides applied |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature of the state |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure of the state |
| `z` | dimensionless | the mixture's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `k` | W/(m*K) | the liquid thermal conductivity |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- the correlation is NeqSim's liquid default (`PFCTConductivityMethodMod86`): a methane SRK reference flash, a Tc/Pc/molar-mass mixing rule, the dilute-gas methane viscosity, the ideal-gas heat capacity, the reference-conductivity correlation and a corresponding-states scaling.
- the reference is pure methane solved with the SRK equation of state; the mixture's own cubic and alpha are not consulted.
- a component's `Tc`, `Pc`, `omega`, every `kij`, its molar mass and its heat-capacity coefficients come from the databank with the keycard's overrides applied.
- this is a liquid-phase correlation; the gas thermal conductivity is `eos.chung_conductivity` / `eos.mason_saxena_conductivity`.

## Cases

| Case | Inputs | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `n_butane_at_250_k_and_1_bar` | components = ['n-butane'], T = 250.0, P = 100000.0, z = [1.0] | k = 0.11961650179494385 |
